MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services are available to members
of our community who require special assistance to participate in public meetings. If you require special assistance,
48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the
hearing impaired, American Sign Language interpreters, a reader during the meeting and/or large print agendas. Please
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information, or request assistance from the staff or
Sergeant-at-Arms at the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: To address the legislative body on items of interest not scheduled for public hearing, Request to
Speak forms will be made available at the meeting and are collected by the staff or Sergeant at Arms. Some legislative
bodies may provide different Request to Speak forms for public hearing items.

AUDIO/VIDEO ACCESS TO BROADCASTED MEETINGS: City Council and Planning Commission meetings are televised live
on HBTV-3 Channel 3, and can be viewed via live or archived website at https://huntingtonbeach.legistar.com.

20.  21-439  Submitted by Mayor Carr - Establish a Recovery Fund to Support

  Fund Program to support local downtown businesses that were impacted by the events
  from the May 21-23 weekend.

21.  21-441  Submitted by Councilmembers Dan Kalmick and Mike Posey -
  Consider agendizing a review of the Settlement Agreement reached

{\*\generator Riched20 5.40.11.2210;}\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Amory Hanson, a candidate for City Council in 2022 and member of the Huntington Beach Historic Resources Board, was called to speak and shared his pleasure at being again allowed to speak in person at this meeting, and requested that all Huntington Beach deliberative assemblies also be allowed to meet in person now.\par
\par
Michael Gates, candidate for reelection as City Attorney in 2022, was called to speak and responded to a recent article in the Orange County Register about an H Item submitted by Councilmembers Posey and Kalmick, and shared factual details on the case.  \par
\par
Cari Swan was called to speak and expressed her appreciation for City Attorney Michael Gates, and summarized her opinion that sensitive legal issues should not be discussed in any open session, but if the Council decides differently, they should start with the 2008 case which is described in the book Friendly Fire: The Illusion of Justice by Adam Bereki, a former Huntington Beach Police Officer.\par
\par
